_strings.@@01ca6b3e8a7f: Child Care Credit (Child and Dependent Care Credit) — Resident individuals who claimed the federal child and dependent care credit. Must attach a copy of federal Form 2441. For spouses who file a joint federal return but separate/combined-separate Delaware returns, the credit may only be applied against the tax of the spouse with the LOWER Line 23 taxable income. This is the child/dependent CARE credit — the federal Child Tax Credit is not an allowable credit on the Delaware return.

_strings.@@5cb8b28cd227: Treaty conformity — DE conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from DE income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the DE return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Delaware's resident return (PIT-RES) starts at Section A, Line 1 = "FEDERAL AGI AMOUNT FROM FEDERAL FORM 1040." Section A - Additions contains ONLY Line 2 (INTEREST ON STATE & LOCAL OBLIGATIONS OTHER THAN DELAWARE) and Line 3 (FIDUCIARY ADJUSTMENT, OIL DEPLETION). There is no add-back of federally treaty-exempt income anywhere in the additions schedule. Because income excluded by treaty is already excluded from federal AGI and Delaware has no treaty add-back, that income flows through untaxed -> conforms. (Source: 2024 Form PIT-RES, Section A, and 2024 PIT-RES instructions.) Note: the resident form's Line 14 "Foreign Taxes Paid" is an itemized-deduction adjustment for those who took the federal Foreign Tax Credit, NOT a treaty-exempt-income add-back.

PO Box 8711, Wilmington, DE 19899-8711"; confirmed by the 2024 PIT-RES Instructions, Line 46 Net Balance Due / Line 47 Net Refund (printed page 11). _strings.@@915d80dc92b3: Earned Income Tax Credit (Delaware EITC) — Resident individuals who claimed (and qualified for) the federal Earned Income Credit. The taxpayer ELECTS one of two options: a REFUNDABLE credit equal to 4.5% of the federal EITC, OR a NONREFUNDABLE credit equal to 20% of the federal EITC. Computed on DE Schedule II (Form PIT-RSS); check the Refundable box on Line 34 if the refundable amount is entered on PIT-RSS Line 16, or Non-Refundable if from PIT-RSS Line 17. Do NOT complete PIT-RSS Schedule II if you did not take the Earned Income Credit on your federal return. For spouses filing separate/combined-separate Delaware returns from a joint federal return, the credit may only be applied against the tax of the spouse with the HIGHER Line 23 taxable income.

_strings.@@d009c3b9f7fc: Form PIT-NON (Delaware Individual Income Tax Return - Non-Resident; formerly Form 200-02). Part-year residents may file either PIT-RES (electing full-year resident treatment) or PIT-NON (electing non-resident treatment), whichever is more advantageous.
_strings.@@e312ca493fad: Credit for Income Taxes Paid to Another State — Delaware residents (or those electing to be taxed as residents) who paid income tax to another state on income earned in that state that is also included in Delaware taxable income. Must attach a signed copy of the other state's return. Does not include city wage taxes or county taxes paid directly to the county; the District of Columbia counts as a 'State' for this credit. Use Form PIT-RSS Schedule I if claiming credit for more than one state (list states highest-to-lowest credit).
_strings.@@eb71823a243b: Multi-state income allocation (which dollars belong to which state) is your and the user's judgment; this tool scopes the returns and supplies the rules/warnings, not the allocation.
_strings.@@ef388cf21371: Personal Credits (exemption credit) — Resident individuals are allowed a credit for each personal exemption. If you were not required to file a federal return, enter $110 for each spouse reporting income plus $110 for each person who could have been listed as a dependent. NOT available if you are claimed as a dependent on another person's return. The number of personal credits is verified against the federal return with the IRS.
_strings.@@f3a0fa807b8b: Additional Personal Credit (age 60 or over) — Resident taxpayer and/or spouse who were 60 years of age or over on December 31, 2024. Check the appropriate box(es) for self/spouse on Line 27b. This is Delaware's main senior-relief credit on the income-tax return (separate senior relief is also provided via the pension exclusion and the Line 11 persons-60-or-over exclusion, which are income exclusions rather than credits).

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: 2024 Form PIT-RES Line 24: 'TAX LIABILITY FROM TAX RATE TABLE/SCHEDULE (See instructions)'. Line 23: 'TAXABLE INCOME - Subtract Line 22 from Line 12, and compute tax on this amount'. Instructions, Line 24: 'If Line 23 is less than $60,000, use the tax table to compute your tax liability. If line 23 is $60,000 or greater, use the tax schedule at the end of the tax table to compute your tax liability. Enter your tax liability on Line 24.' NOTE — 2024 renumbering: these were Lines 22/23 on the 2023 form. This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: 2024 UNCHANGED TAX / RENUMBERED FORM: the brackets, the $3,250/$6,500 standard deduction, the $2,500 additional standard deduction, and the $110 personal credits are all unchanged from 2023, but the 2024 PIT-RES renumbered the lines — the deduction election is Line 20 (was 19a), additional standard deduction Line 21 (was 20), total deductions Line 22 (was 21), TAXABLE INCOME Line 23 (was 22), TAX LIABILITY Line 24 (was 23), and the personal credits moved to Lines 27a/27b (were 26a/26b). Use the 2024 line numbers when reading amounts off the form. Base guidance: Supply 2024 Form PIT-RES Line 12, DELAWARE ADJUSTED GROSS INCOME = Line 1 federal AGI (from federal Form 1040) + Section A additions (Line 2 interest on non-Delaware state/local obligations; Line 3 fiduciary adjustment / oil depletion) - Section B subtractions (Line 5 U.S.-obligation interest; Line 6 pension/retirement exclusions; Line 7 Delaware state tax refund, fiduciary adjustment, work opportunity credit, Delaware NOL carryforward; Line 8a taxable Social Security / Railroad Retirement benefits, higher-education exclusion, certain lump-sum distributions; Line 8b 529/ABLE contribution deduction) - Line 11 exclusion for certain persons 60 and over or disabled. If the filer has no Delaware additions or subtractions, Line 12 equals federal AGI. The op then subtracts the shipped per-status standard deduction to reproduce Line 23 taxable income (Line 23 = Line 12 - Line 22 total deductions). NO income-based exemptions are shipped (exemptions = {}): Delaware's per-person allowances are TAX CREDITS, not subtractions from income. 2024 Form PIT-RES Line 27a Personal Credits = $110 x the number of exemptions ('Enter number of exemptions' [a box] 'x $110'; e.g., MFJ with no dependents = $220), and Line 27b Additional Personal Credits = $110 per taxpayer/spouse age 60 or over on December 31, 2024 — both are subtracted from the Line 26 tax, not from income. They are NOT applied by calc.state_tax; claim them on the form. exemptions_count and dependents_count must therefore be 0 for this pack. A filer claimed as a dependent on another person's return gets $0 personal credit. SINGLE rate schedule for ALL filing statuses: 30 Del. C. sec. 1102(a)(14) publishes one rate table with no filing-status variation, and the 2024 State Income Tax Table has no filing-status columns; the schedule is duplicated per status here. Only the standard deduction differs by status ($6,500 Filing Status 2 vs $3,250 Statuses 1, 3, 4, 5). TAX TABLE MANDATE below $60,000 — bracket math may differ by a few dollars within table bands; the filed form must use the table: 'If Line 23 is less than $60,000, use the tax table to compute your tax liability' (Line 24 instructions). The 2024 table uses $50-wide bands; sampled band values reproduce midpoint bracket math exactly (taxable $26,550-$26,600: table $1,088 vs midpoint math $1,088.41 -> $1,088; $10,100-$10,150: $267; $2,200-$2,250: $5). At $60,000 or over the printed schedule ($2,943.50 + 6.60% of the portion over $60,000) IS exact marginal math. Printed-constant check (re-derived for 2024): the schedule's $2,943.50 at $60,000 exactly equals the cumulative sum of the prior brackets (0.022 x 3,000 = 66.00; + 0.039 x 5,000 = 195.00; + 0.048 x 10,000 = 480.00; + 0.052 x 5,000 = 260.00; + 0.0555 x 35,000 = 1,942.50; total 2,943.50) — no divergence. Provenance of the sub-$60,000 rates: the 2024 DOR booklet and tax-table PDF print a rate schedule ONLY for taxable income of $60,000 or over (below that they mandate the table). The 2.2%/3.9%/4.8%/5.2%/5.55% marginal rates and their $2,000/$5,000/$10,000/$20,000/$25,000/$60,000 breakpoints are copied from 30 Del. C. sec. 1102(a)(14) (official Delaware Code site, taxable years beginning after December 31, 2013 — re-fetched live and unchanged for 2024) and cross-check exactly against the DOR table's band values and the printed $2,943.50 constant. The first bracket is a zero-rate floor: sec. 1102(a)(14) imposes no tax on the first $2,000 of taxable income (the rate schedule starts at '2.2% of taxable income in excess of $2,000'), and the 2024 tax table shows $0 tax for taxable income under $2,000. Additional standard deduction NOT applied by the engine: Line 21 allows $2,500 per box checked for taxpayer/spouse age 65 or over and/or blind (maximum $5,000 per individual), ONLY for filers electing the Delaware standard deduction ('If you elect to itemize your deductions, you do not qualify for the additional standard deduction'). Enter it on the form; the shipped standard_deduction covers Line 20a only. Itemizers: the standard deduction is in lieu of itemizing. Filers may itemize on the Delaware return (Section C Lines 13-19 + Form PIT-RSA, checked on Line 20b) even if they took the federal standard deduction; the shipped standard_deduction applies only to standard-deduction electors. For Filing Status 3 or 4, if one spouse itemizes the other must itemize; if one takes the standard deduction the other must too. Delaware filing statuses are 1 Single/Divorced/Widow(er); 2 Married Filing Joint; 3 Married Filing Separate Forms; 4 Married Filing Combined Separate (two separate computations in Columns A and B of one form, $3,250 standard deduction per column); 5 Head of Household. The engine's married_filing_separately corresponds to Status 3 or per-column Status 4 (both $3,250). QUALIFYING SURVIVING SPOUSE caution: the engine maps QSS to married_filing_jointly ($6,500 standard deduction), but the PIT-RES Filing Status 1 covers 'Single, Divorced, Widow(er)' and the 2024 booklet never mentions the federal QSS status. A widow(er) not remarried at year-end appears to file Delaware Status 1 ($3,250 standard deduction) — the brackets are identical either way, but the deduction differs by $3,250. Confirm the correct Delaware status at revenue.delaware.gov before relying on the QSS->MFJ mapping. Tax on lump-sum distributions is NOT modeled: 2024 Form PIT-RES Line 25 adds a separate tax on qualified lump-sum distributions computed on Form PIT-STC (30 Del. C. sec. 1102(b) separate tax); the engine computes Line 24 only (Line 26 TOTAL TAX = Line 24 + Line 25). Base subtractions taken BEFORE Line 12 are the caller's responsibility: the pension/retirement exclusion (Line 6), the exclusion for certain persons 60 and over or disabled (Line 11), the DE 529/ABLE contribution deduction (Line 8b — 529 max $1,000 single-type filers under $100,000 federal AGI / $2,000 joint under $200,000; ABLE max $5,000/$10,000), U.S.-obligation interest (Line 5), and taxable Social Security / Railroad Retirement benefits (Line 8a) — supply Line 12 Delaware AGI already reflecting them. Delaware EITC (elect refundable 4.5% or nonrefundable 20% of federal EITC, Line 34), child care credit (50% of federal Form 2441 Line 11, max $3,000, Line 31), other-state credit (Line 28), volunteer firefighter credit ($1,000, Line 29), and the $110 personal credits (Lines 27a/27b) are all CREDITS against tax — none of them are exemptions and none are modeled by this op. Rounding: 'Dollar amounts on your return must be rounded off to the nearest whole dollar. This means that amounts from 50 to 99 cents are increased to the next dollar' — matches the engine's half-up rounding. The 2024 tax-schedule example rounds $3,455.06 to $3,455. No local income tax is collected on Form PIT-RES (the return has no local/county tax line). Part-year residents may elect to file either PIT-RES (full-year resident treatment) or PIT-NON, whichever is more advantageous; this pack models the resident form PIT-RES.
